evidence.observation: Small carrier owner (runs drivers; 'Dispatch was literally begging receivers') says a 2-drop load was unloaded 24 hours late, they politely asked the broker for detention/layover 'and nothing happens'; asks for tactics. Page opened 2026-10-27.

Owner-operator: brokers look for excuses not to pay; he emails notice as proof, but even after billing detention with BOL in/out times a large broker paid linehaul only, so he had to call their billing department and wait on hold 'too long for a normal guy'; another broker paid only after a lengthy email. Page opened 2026-10-27.

Expedite team contractor leased to a carrier: detention is inconsistent, sometimes paid and sometimes not; a 12+ hour border delay caused by a broker paperwork error paid only a $25 bump; 'we do not know until the run is complete if D-time will be paid at all'. Leased contractor, not an own-authority carrier. Page opened 2026-10-27.
Same carrier owner adds they usually have smooth operations and are just trying to recover something to compensate the driver. Page opened 2026-10-27.

SNIPPET (search excerpt only, page not opened per project rule): commenter claims most owner-operators he knows 'would pay low double digits' for something that got detention unstuck; second-hand willingness-to-pay claim. Comment id not visible.

Dispatch service page: 5% of gross for one truck (4% fleets, 7% new MC); included in the percentage: 'Detention and layover claims, chased until they're paid or closed out'; dispatcher also books loads and runs broker calls; example week $6,000 gross -> $300 fee. Rate con still goes to and is signed by the carrier. Page opened 2026-10-27; undated.

Dispatch contract guide: 'A 7 percent fee on $300 of detention pay is $21. Across 10 loads with detention per month, that is $210/month' that carriers pay dispatchers on detention alone. Worked example by the publisher (ESTIMATE basis for budget), not a survey. Page opened 2026-10-27.

Dispatch firm guide: collection process is a separate detention invoice with rate con, arrival/departure photos, ELD records and amount, submitted within 48 hours, followed up at 7 and 14 days; says solo operators booking few loads with a broker 'often get ghosted'. Page opened 2026-10-27.

root_cause.mechanism: Self-dispatched small carriers already capture times and notice, but detention claims die afterwards: the claim is not submitted promptly with matching documents, and nobody chases broker accounts payable, so the broker pays linehaul only.

intervention.mechanism: Back-office detention desk: the carrier forwards the rate con, BOL and ELD timestamps after delivery; the desk sends the detention invoice within 48 hours and follows up with broker AP in writing at 7 and 14 days until paid or formally denied. The carrier keeps booking its own loads.

submit detention invoices and follow up with broker AP on the carrier's behalf

validation.hypothesis: Self-dispatched 1-3 truck carriers will pay a refundable $49 deposit to hand off detention follow-up.
validation.method: One offer page plus written forum posts and emails to carriers (copy approved and sent by Matteo); no calls; count paid refundable deposits only.
validation.success: >= 3 paid refundable $49 deposits from distinct carriers within 14 days
validation.kill: <= 1 paid deposit within 14 days, or depositors forward 0 claims within 30 days
